```{r import-data} 
# Load required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)
library(e1071)
library(factoextra) # For PCA visualization

# Define column names based on dataset documentation
col_names <- c("id", "diagnosis", 
               paste0(rep(c("radius", "texture", "perimeter", "area", "smoothness", 
                            "compactness", "concavity", "concave_points", "symmetry", 
                            "fractal_dimension"), 3), 
                      rep(c("_mean", "_se", "_worst"), each = 10)))

# 1. Import data
# Assuming your R project is open, we navigate to the data folder
wdbc <- read_csv("../data/wdbc.data", col_names = col_names)

# 2. Quality Control and Cleaning
# Remove the ID column as it holds no predictive value, and convert diagnosis to a factor
wdbc_clean <- wdbc %>%
  select(-id) %>%
  mutate(diagnosis = factor(diagnosis, levels = c("B", "M"), labels = c("Benign", "Malignant")))

# Check for missing values (QC)
sum(is.na(wdbc_clean)) # Should be 0 
``` 
```{r eda}
# Class distribution plot
ggplot(wdbc_clean, aes(x = diagnosis, fill = diagnosis)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Benign vs Malignant Tumors", x = "Diagnosis", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
# We exclude the first column (diagnosis) and scale the numeric variables
pca_res <- prcomp(wdbc_clean[, -1], scale. = TRUE)

# Visualize PCA
fviz_pca_ind(pca_res,
             geom.ind = "point", 
             col.ind = wdbc_clean$diagnosis, 
             palette = c("#00AFBB", "#FC4E07"),
             addEllipses = TRUE, 
             legend.title = "Diagnosis",
             title = "PCA of Breast Cancer Features") 
```
